President Trump on Friday told reporters in the Oval Office that he will "demand" that companies that make childhood vaccines manufacture doses that are significantly smaller than currently recommended to cut autism rates.
Speaking at a press conference about
"Most Favored Nation" drug pricing to Medicaid recipients in all states, Trump said a recommendation will be made to give childhood vaccines through five shots spaced six-months apart.
The president noted that the change would lead to a “massive reduction” in autism cases.

Prominent scientific organizations, citing studies, have repeatedly stated that there is no relationship between vaccines and autism. "This has been confirmed through dozens of scientific studies examining different types of vaccines and different vaccine timing schedules," the Autism Science Foundation says.
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been a long-time skeptic of vaccines and has not rejected the vaccines-autism link.

title: Trump to 'demand' vaccine makers make smaller doses for kids to address autism
